title: Model-written summary of an analysis packet
description: The llm-summary.json holding prose written over one kafkars.analysis-packet.v1, and bound to it. A language model is useful here for saying in readable English what a packet of numbers means; it is not useful for deciding what the numbers are, and this document is shaped so that it cannot. Every quantitative claim is a reference into the packet's metrics, every citation is a reference into the packet's evidence_refs, and the verdict is copied rather than concluded. LlmSummary::validate_against enforces all three mechanically, and rejecting a summary costs nothing because the numbers never depended on the prose. Documentation mirror of the LlmSummary serde type in crates/bench-schema/src/llm.rs, which is the source of truth.

verdict.description: The packet's verdict, copied verbatim. A summary whose verdict differs from its packet's is rejected: prose may elaborate on the deterministic layer, never overrule it.

executive_summary.description: What happened, in a paragraph a reader can act on. A summary that says nothing is not a summary.

findings.description: Statements about the evidence, each citing the packet. Every metric_refs entry must name a key the packet's metrics defines, and every evidence_refs entry a key its evidence_refs defines.

hypotheses.description: Proposed explanations, each labeled with how much weight it carries so that speculation cannot be mistaken for a finding.

confidence.description: low: a guess worth writing down. medium: consistent with the evidence, not established by it. high: strongly indicated, still not something the packet asserts.

next_experiments.description: Experiments that would settle what this one did not.

caveats.description: What a reader must not conclude from this summary.
